identified_problem: GHD is a global professional services company that grew from a small engineering practice founded in Melbourne, Australia, in 1928, and today provides integrated digital, engineering, environmental, design and construction services. The 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires and the 2022 NSW/Queensland floods have intensified demand for hazard-aware planning, asset resilience and environmental risk advice across the Australian infrastructure, water, energy and built-environment projects that GHD advises on.
climate_exposure: Its Australian project portfolio spans transport, water, energy, property and environmental advisory work in regions repeatedly affected by wildfire, flood, drought and heat.
potential_pain: Clients increasingly require defensible climate-risk inputs for design standards, environmental approvals and business-case assumptions; without granular hazard data, GHD risks higher professional-indemnity exposure and lost advisory mandates.
evidence: Address-level wildfire and flood exposure layers plus historical event intelligence for the 2019–20 Black Summer and 2022 eastern-Australia floods, relevant to GHD’s Australian infrastructure and environment advisory work.
recommended_message: Show GHD how Talaix wildfire and flood exposure layers can underpin hazard screening, design briefs and environmental approvals for Australian infrastructure clients.
fit_score: GHD’s Australian heritage, multidisciplinary project footprint and explicit environment advisory capability make it a natural channel for embedding Talaix hazard analytics into client-facing engineering and environmental work.

interactions.summary: Identified via official-source research; signal: GHD’s official site states it grew from a Melbourne engineering practice in 1928 into a global professional services firm offering environmental, engineering and design services.
